clue.text: A wheeler-dealer, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase tells the solver the word for the clue's cyclist is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: someone who wheels along on a bike is a pedaller

explanation.surface: A slick business operator described as someone who sounds like a wheeler-dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated phrase splits in two: 'wheeler' is a pedaller (a cyclist), and said aloud that sounds like the word for a 'dealer', which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawker who goes about selling small goods is a kind of trader or seller.

clue.text: But Arctic fur doesn't come from it

definitions.text: But Arctic fur doesn't come from it

parts.words: But Arctic fur doesn't come from it
parts.note: the animal's name sounds as if it were a cat from the North Pole, yet its fur is not Arctic at all

explanation.surface: A remark that some fur is not Arctic in origin.
explanation.walkthrough: The name suggests a 'cat' from the 'pole', which would make its fur Arctic; in fact the animal is a European weasel relative.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a dark-furred mustelid of temperate Europe, nothing to do with the polar regions despite its name.

clue.text: He argues that a large animal swallows a small one

indicators.note: one creature swallowing another means the second word goes inside the first

parts.note: a deer is a sizeable animal
a bat is a small animal

explanation.surface: Someone claims that a big beast gobbles up a little one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes part in a formal debate puts forward arguments.

clue.text: Song's words upset Cyril

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the name are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Cyril is upset by the words of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: The words of a song are its lyric, the text set to music.

clue.text: The last runners try to be first in it

definitions.text: The last runners try to be first in it

parts.words: The last runners try to be first in it
parts.note: the final runners on each team are the anchors who try to cross the line ahead after taking over the baton

explanation.surface: A paradox about runners at the back trying to come first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last runners' sounds like stragglers, but means each team's final leg runner in a team event.
explanation.definitionFit: A team race in which runners each cover a leg in turn, handing on a baton.

clue.text: Keep us confined in a bad spot

indicators.note: something confined in another is held inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a stain is a bad spot or blemish
taken as written

explanation.surface: We are stuck in an awkward place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bad spot' reads like a tight corner, but here it is a mark or blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to maintain or keep it going.

clue.text: Old-fashioned engine set out before morning

indicators.note: before places the rearranged letters ahead of the next piece
out here means put out of order, so the three letters are rearranged

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: A vintage locomotive sets off early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam power drove the engines of an earlier age, so the word stands for that old kind of engine.

clue.text: Directors of the railway

parts.note: reads like a company's board, but means the staff who direct trains by working signals

explanation.surface: The board of directors of a railway company.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway signal-box workers control and direct the movement of trains.

clue.text: Insect swallows fruit for nourishment

indicators.note: one thing swallowing another means the second goes inside the first

parts.note: an ant is an insect
a lime is a fruit

explanation.surface: A bug eats some fruit to feed itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for food or sustenance.

clue.text: Failure of phone or exchange

indicators.note: exchange means the letters swap places with one another, giving a new order

explanation.surface: A breakdown of the telephone or the exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange' looks like a telephone exchange, but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with no chance of success is a dud or loser.

clue.text: Free with a political party

definitions.meaning: free in the sense of generous or open-handed, or not strict
the British party formerly called by this name

explanation.surface: Unrestricted, and belonging to a party of politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous and unrestricted describe a liberal attitude; the historic British Whig successor party bore the same name.

clue.text: Sidespin for billiard-players from America and from England

definitions.meaning: in American pool and billiards, spin put on a ball by hitting it off-centre goes by this name
native to or coming from England

explanation.surface: Spin used by American cue-sport players, and also something English.
explanation.walkthrough: In American usage the word, lowercase, means side spin on a cue ball; the British call it 'side'.
explanation.definitionFit: American cue players call side spin by this name; otherwise the word simply means belonging to England.

clue.text: A number stay calm in upheaval

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number

indicators.note: the words stay calm are in a jumbled state, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Several people keep their cool during a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' is the Roman numeral C (100), not a crowd of people; STAY CALM is then rearranged to follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataclysm is a violent upheaval or catastrophe.

clue.text: One old car in a pile up

parts.note: A means one, as in a single thing
a heap is slang for a battered old car

explanation.surface: A single old car caught in a motorway pile-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pile up' reads as a crash, but the definition is the adverb 'in a pile', heaped up.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adverb means heaped together, piled in a mass.

clue.text: Cast worth putting into new production

indicators.note: staging the word afresh, as in a new production of a play, means rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: The actors are worth staging in a new show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the actors of a play, but here it is the verb meaning to fling.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast something is to fling or hurl it.

clue.text: A crew sick at sea? That's a joke!

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are shuffled around

explanation.surface: A ship's crew falling ill on the ocean is the punchline.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisecrack is a witty quip or gag.

clue.text: About time to correct the height indicator

indicators.note: about here means going around, so the word for correct surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to alter something is to correct or amend it
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is high time the height gauge was fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: An altimeter is an instrument showing altitude, as in an aircraft.

clue.text: Persuade one to discuss without coming to any conclusions

definitions.meaning: to bring someone round to your view by talking

definitions.text: discuss without coming to any conclusions
definitions.meaning: to talk around a subject without ever tackling or settling it

explanation.surface: Win someone over by chatting without ever reaching a decision.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the phrasal verb: persuading someone over, or circling a topic while avoiding its heart.

clue.text: Surprise with one missile coming after another

indicators.note: the second missile comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: a bomb is an explosive missile
a shell is another kind of explosive missile

explanation.surface: A shock as one projectile follows another.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of shattering news is called by the name of an explosive shell.

clue.text: How schoolboys are punished and journalists recognised

definitions.meaning: schoolchildren are punished by being made to write out lines
a journalist is credited by the name line above an article

explanation.surface: How pupils get punished and reporters get credited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' is a British school punishment: writing out the same sentence many times.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, the phrase gives the punishment; as one, the line naming an article's writer.

clue.text: A limit I set for force in emergency

indicators.note: set means arranged, so the letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone sets a limit on what force may be used.
explanation.definitionFit: A civilian reserve army called up in a crisis is a militia.

clue.text: Plane crash in the Himalayas

indicators.note: a crash wrecks the word, rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: An aircraft goes down in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of where the country lies, a Himalayan kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The country lies along the mountain range between India and Tibet.

clue.text: Crossing the channel

definitions.meaning: a sea voyage or journey across
a narrow way or route through, like a corridor or duct

explanation.surface: Sailing across the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A voyage across water is a passage, and so is a narrow way through something.

clue.text: Possibly learns about key cavalrymen

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
possibly signals that the letters could form another word, so they are rearranged

parts.note: C is a musical key

explanation.surface: Maybe someone learns about an important point concerning horse soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancers were mounted soldiers armed with lances.

clue.text: Colour I call unusual

indicators.note: unusual means out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says they name an odd shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale purple shade.

clue.text: People in serious offence

parts.note: mortals are human beings
taken as written

explanation.surface: Folk involved in a grave crime.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic teaching a grave wrong that destroys grace is called this sin.

clue.text: Fruit of lemon variety

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A type of fruit from a lemon cultivar.
explanation.definitionFit: A melon is a large juicy fruit.

clue.text: Story-teller for soap set around English capital

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the next piece
set means arranged, so the letters are put in a new order
the capital of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A soap opera set in the capital of England needs a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' suggests where a soap takes place, but signals the rearrangement; 'English capital' is its first letter, not London.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek teller of fables.

clue.text: Getting a goal is the name of this game

definitions.text: Getting a goal is the name of this game

parts.words: Getting a goal is the name of this game
parts.note: scoring means putting the ball through the net, and the sport's name says just that

explanation.surface: Scoring is what this sport is all about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the name of this game' is the idiom for the main point, but literally the name describes scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team game where goals are scored by putting the ball through a high net.

clue.text: Go back to score an advantage over a fellow-player?

definitions.text: Go back to score an advantage over a fellow-player?

parts.words: Go back to score an advantage over a fellow-player?
parts.note: an actor moving to the rear of the stage forces others to turn away from the audience, stealing the scene

explanation.surface: An actor retreats to get the better of a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshine a fellow performer, originally by moving to the rear of the stage.

clue.text: In certain ways, you don't have to ease off

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: S, E and N are compass directions, ways one can go
to lack is not to have

explanation.surface: In some respects, there is no need to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'certain ways' are three compass points: South, East and North.
explanation.definitionFit: To slacken is to loosen or reduce effort.

clue.text: Birds providing thrills at fairgrounds

definitions.meaning: the dipper is a small bird of fast streams

explanation.surface: Birds that offer the excitement of a funfair ride.
explanation.walkthrough: A big dipper is the British name for a roller coaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Dippers are stream-diving songbirds, and also roller-coaster rides.
